A.why: Sequential updates and transaction rollback provide a straightforward approach, but conflict handling continues after failures, lookups remain app-wide, and no tests are added.

B.why: Per-operation planning clearly separates conflict checks from writes and respects reverse execution order, but introduces repeated queries and substantial nesting without regression tests.

C.why: Preserving deferred writes is reasonable, but coordinating database results with mutable dictionary records adds complexity while leaving reverse operation ordering and regression coverage unaddressed.

D.why: A concise model-level chain collapse fits the existing planning structure and includes forward/backward integration coverage, though case normalization and reversal within a migration remain unaddressed.

E.why: Transactional stepwise processing is understandable and reverses operations appropriately, but retains ambiguous action-prefix matching and app-wide conflict checks without adding tests.

F.why: The explicit per-step plan and explanatory comment make sequential processing clear, but repeated database work and app-wide conflict detection lack supporting regression tests.

G.why: In-memory planning avoids intermediate writes and includes integration coverage, but indexing an entire app by codename discards content-type distinctions and reverse operation ordering remains untreated.

H.why: Model-level collapsing and forward/backward integration tests are useful, but redundant ordering structures complicate the implementation while case normalization and reversal within a migration remain unaddressed.
